questions.text: Why multiply each audio frame by a Hann window before computing its Fourier transform?

options.A: To map uniformly spaced frequency bins onto the mel scale.
options.B: To compress large differences in spectral magnitude logarithmically.
options.C: To reduce spectral leakage by tapering the frame boundaries.
options.D: To decorrelate mel features into a smaller set of coefficients.

questions.explanation: Tapering the frame boundaries reduces discontinuities at the edges, which reduces spectral leakage.

questions.text: Training used 80 log-mel features with per-utterance normalization. Inference uses 128 features with global normalization. What should you do first?

options.A: Match the inference feature settings to the training pipeline.
options.B: Pad the trained model output with 48 extra feature values.
options.C: Increase the inference audio amplitude to compensate for the mismatch.
options.D: Apply a DCT at inference without changing the training features.

questions.explanation: Feature dimensions and normalization must match the trained frontend; different settings change the model input representation.

questions.text: The framing code uses n = 1 + (len(signal) - frame_len) // hop and keeps only those full frames. For len(signal) = 1000, frame_len = 400, and hop = 160, how many frames does it return?
questions.explanation: Integer division gives 600 // 160 = 3, so n = 4; starts are 0, 160, 320, and 480.
